steps.name: QC and paired DESeq2 differential expression
caveats: With n=5 pairs, statistical power is limited; report effect sizes and confidence alongside p-values rather than relying on padj cutoff alone
If any subject is missing a control or treated sample (11 count columns vs 10 metadata rows), resolve/report the mismatch before modeling
steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts from STAR/featureCounts, 12000 genes x 11 samples (one column is likely gene ID; 10 sample columns for 5 subjects x 2 conditions). Metadata table has 10 rows with subject and condition columns confirming the paired design. This is the primary DE step answering the core research question.
steps.question: Within the paired control-vs-treated blood samples from 5 subjects, which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated and control conditions after accounting for subject-to-subject variability?
constraints: Use the paired/blocked design ~subject + condition in DESeq2, not an unpaired two-group model, since the biology and metadata both indicate matched control/treated samples per subject
Verify sample name alignment between counts.csv columns and metadata.csv rows before building the DESeqDataSet
Do not drop the subject term from the model even if it costs degrees of freedom — it is required to isolate the within-subject treatment effect
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12000 genes x samples) and metadata (10 rows: subject, condition) are loaded and sample identifiers are matched/aligned between the two files
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g. require a minimum count sum or CPM threshold across samples) before dispersion estimation
DESeq2 is run with design ~subject + condition (paired/blocked design), condition releveled so 'control' is the reference level

Output includes a full results table (log2FoldChange, lfcSE, p-value, padj) for all tested genes, independent filtering applied, and log2FoldChange shrinkage (apeglm or ashr) reported alongside raw estimates
Significant gene list (padj < 0.05) is exported with counts of up- and down-regulated genes
PCA or sample-distance plot is produced to confirm paired subject clustering and check for outlier samples/batch effects before trusting the DE calls

steps.name: Per-subject visualization of treatment response
caveats: With only 5 subjects, apparent per-subject heterogeneity may simply reflect small-sample noise rather than true biological heterogeneity
steps.context: Builds directly on the DESeq2 results and variance-stabilized counts from T1S1 to give a per-subject view of the treatment response, since the research question is framed at the level of individual subjects.
steps.question: Is the treatment-associated gene expression change from the paired DESeq2 model consistent across all 5 subjects, or driven by one or two outlier subjects?
constraints: Use variance-stabilizing transformation (vst or rlog) from the same DESeqDataSet fit in T1S1, do not re-normalize independently
acceptance_criteria: Volcano plot and MA plot of the paired DE results are generated
Heatmap of normalized (variance-stabilized) expression for the top significant genes (e.g. top 30-50 by padj) is generated with samples ordered/grouped by subject and condition
Per-gene paired line plots (control -> treated per subject) are produced for the top 10-20 significant genes to visually confirm within-subject direction of change
Any subject whose response direction disagrees with the majority for the top genes is flagged in the output summary

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: Pathway enrichment on a small (n=5 pairs) paired study reflects the same limited power as the underlying DE call; treat enriched pathways as hypothesis-generating
steps.context: Uses the WikiPathways human pathway gene sets (GMT, HGNC symbols, confirmed present at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt) to interpret the paired DE gene list biologically. Gene symbols in counts.csv must be matched to HGNC symbols used in the GMT; if counts use Ensembl IDs, map to symbols first.
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human biological pathways are enriched among the genes significantly changed by treatment (paired analysis) in these blood samples?
constraints: Match the organism-specific WikiPathways human gene set to this human blood dataset only
If gene identifiers in the counts matrix are not HGNC symbols, perform ID mapping before enrichment rather than skipping unmatched genes silently
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment is run on the significant gene set (padj < 0.05) from T1S1, using a background of all genes tested (post-filtering) as the universe
A ranked-list (GSEA-style, pre-ranked on the DESeq2 test statistic or shrunken log2FoldChange) enrichment is also run across all tested genes to capture sub-threshold coordinated pathway shifts
Enriched pathways are reported with adjusted p-values (BH/FDR), normalized enrichment scores where applicable, and the member gene overlap for each significant pathway
Report explicitly states if the WikiPathways human gene-set reference was unavailable and enrichment could not run

plan.title: Paired treatment vs control DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts (12000 genes x 11 samples) for a paired design: 5 human blood subjects, each contributing a control and a treated sample (10 samples used; metadata has 10 rows x 3 columns capturing subject and condition). Because samples are paired within subject, the correct model is a paired DESeq2 design (~subject + condition) rather than an unpaired two-group comparison, which controls for inter-subject variability and directly answers 'which genes respond to treatment within each subject'. The plan: (1) QC and paired-aware normalization/DE with DESeq2 modeling subject as a blocking factor and condition as the effect of interest, (2) diagnostic visualization of the paired response (MA plot, volcano, per-subject heatmap of top DE genes) to confirm the treatment effect is consistent across subjects, (3) functional interpretation of the significant gene set via WikiPathways human pathway enrichment. No survival/PK/translational data are present, so no downstream translational tracks are added.
